summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a regular expression.
description: `nonRegExp(value)` is the same test as `!isRegExp(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Identified by its internal tag rather than by `instanceof`, so a regular expression from another frame is recognised too.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a regular expression; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonRegExp("/a/"); // => true
nonRegExp({}); // => true
nonRegExp(null); // => true
nonRegExp(/a/); // => false
nonRegExp(new RegExp("a")); // => false
```
